title: Raymond Lifestyle Ltd - 544240 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Raymond Lifestyle Q1 FY27 total income rose 6% to INR1,560 crore, EBITDA up 11% to INR135 crore at 8.6% margin, net cash surplus INR154 crore.
summary.overview: Total income grew 6% YoY to INR1,560 crore and EBITDA rose 11% to INR135 crore, with margin up 40 bps to 8.6%. Garmenting was the standout, with revenue up 50% to INR296 crore and EBITDA turning positive at INR22 crore. Branded Apparel grew only 4% and Branded Textiles fell about 2%, mainly on base effects and adverse channel and product mix. Management called FY27 a year of consolidation, with net store closures continuing for two to three more quarters, and said Q1 was ahead of budget.

segments.name: Branded Textiles
segments.commentary: Revenue INR684 crore vs INR699 crore YoY on base effect from a large prior-year fabric quarter; EBITDA INR95 crore vs INR107 crore, margin 13.9% on scale deleverage.

segments.name: Branded Apparel (four core brands)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR349 crore, +4% YoY, with LFS and e-commerce growing high double digits (LFS above 25%); EBITDA INR18 crore, margin 5.1% on adverse channel mix.

segments.name: Garmenting
segments.commentary: Revenue INR296 crore vs INR197 crore, +50% YoY on US tariff rationalisation and new UK/EU clients; EBITDA INR22 crore vs negative INR8 crore, margin 7.3% vs -4.1%.

segments.name: High Value Cotton Shirting
segments.commentary: Revenue INR195 crore vs INR205 crore YoY on base effect; EBITDA steady at INR19 crore, margin 9.7% vs 9.1%.

segments.name: Emerging Businesses (Ethnix, Raymond Home, innerwear, Chairman's Collection, sexual wellness)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR79 crore, +9% YoY; now reported as a standalone segment after reclassification. Ethnix net stores down 17 in the quarter.

guidance_outlook: Management is bullish on FY27 and said Q1 is ahead of budget phasing and ahead of last year; Q2 described as decent.
Garmenting capacity is full through December; orders booked from January onwards. Management said no risk to margins on cost-plus contracts, though changes in Sep-Oct could affect pricing.
Price hikes to start in Q2: management estimates 5-7% in apparel and 7-9% in fabric, calibrated against volumes.

Medium term: aim to at least double turnover in five years and grow EBITDA faster than revenue, before any Kearney-led transformation outcomes. Mid-teens ROCE described as the endeavour, not a target. Garmenting EBITDA double-digit described as an endeavour with no firm timeline.
Net branded EBO openings to be negative in FY27; EBO closures expected to take another 2-3 quarters.
capex_capacity: Garmenting: five factories (three in Karnataka, one new in Andhra Pradesh, one in Ethiopia); no spare capacity until December per management. Company has 11 factories in total.
Active network 1,627 stores across 600 cities. Since June 2025, 133 stores exited and 85 opened.
Branded EBOs in Q1: 8 opened, 24 closed (net -16). TRS format net +6. Ethnix: 1 opened, 18 closed (net -17). Management said EBO network is down 34 net (9%).
Renewable energy share in factories around 12% this year vs 8-9% last year; target 25% by 2030, which management expects to reach early.
Ethnix plan: shift sherwanis and bandhgalas above INR50,000 to made-to-measure; basic kurtas to be sold through TRS and e-commerce; high-impact flagship stores in wedding areas.
demand_pricing: Garmenting US share fell to 55% under tariffs and has recovered to 59-60%; UK rose from 10% to 12% and Europe from 6% to 7-8%. Management aims to bring US to about 55%.
New clients named: El Corte Ingles (Spain), OVS (Italy), Carl Gross (Germany), T.M. Lewin (UK, shirting). UK FTA live from 15 July; EU FTA expected to take 6-9 months to take effect.

Branded apparel: management attributed the weak quarter to Adhik Maas (about one month without auspicious buying) and delayed festive dates by 20-25 days. Casual brands (ColorPlus, Parx) growing double digit; casual share in Park Avenue and Raymond Ready-to-Wear reached about 18%.
Retail: TRS stores up 5-6% and EBOs up 3% like-for-like. Management said premium-end off-take in Q1 was not an issue.
Raw material inflation YoY: wool about +100%, cotton and flax about +20%, chemicals about +30%. Gross margin was held despite this because Q1 sold at forward-booked prices.

qa_highlights.question: Input cost pressure in fabric and textiles, and how price hikes or inventory efficiency will offset it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited wool, flax, cotton, dyes and chemicals as rising costs. Mitigation includes new vendors, Make in India sourcing, freight consolidation, and a cost transformation project. Price increases to begin in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Garmenting outlook and whether contracts allow pass-through of RM costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Orders are cost-plus, and bookings for January onward are open with December capacity full. Higher plant utilisation is expected to help margins. Management declined to give firm double-digit EBITDA guidance, citing unpredictable international trade conditions.

qa_highlights.question: Depreciation rise of about 25%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR11 crore was a one-time lease-accounting error from last year and will not recur, so it can be excluded from run-rate depreciation.

qa_highlights.question: Store rationalisation timeline and Ethnix store additions?
qa_highlights.answer: Closures will take another 2-3 quarters, so FY27 net branded EBO openings will be negative. Ethnix will shift top-end products to made-to-measure and move basic lines to TRS and e-commerce, with flagship stores in wedding areas.

qa_highlights.question: Medium-term revenue, margin and ROCE targets?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims to at least double turnover and grow EBITDA faster than revenue in five years, before any Kearney-led project outcomes. Mid-teens ROCE is described as a good outcome for a manufacturing business, not a target.

qa_highlights.question: Which brands drive casualisation, and what are the branded apparel and export order trends?
qa_highlights.answer: Branded apparel grew 4% due to EBO closures, with e-commerce and LFS growing high double digits. Order books span Europe, US, Japan, Korea and Asia. Management said FY28 is not being looked at closely.

risks_watch: Store closures: management says EBO closures need another 2-3 quarters, with FY27 net branded EBO openings negative; monitor net EBO count (down 34, about 9%) and whether closures stay on this timeline.

Raw material inflation: wool about +100%, cotton and flax about +20%, chemicals about +30% YoY; Q1 margins relied on forward-booked prices, so Q2 onwards depends on price hikes of 5-7% in apparel and 7-9% in fabric holding volumes.

Garmenting visibility: capacity full through December with bookings from January; management declined firm double-digit EBITDA guidance, citing unpredictable US tariff and Middle East developments, and Sep-Oct cost moves could affect cost-plus pricing.
Branded apparel: revenue +4% YoY and EBITDA margin 5.1%; recovery relies on festive and wedding dates shifting 20-25 days into H2, with Adhik Maas hitting Q1 suit off-take.

Depreciation normalisation: exclude INR11 crore one-off lease-accounting item from run-rate; watch depreciation and ROCE, which management said will take time to improve as stores and capacity are added.
Ethnix repositioning to made-to-measure and high-impact flagships; watch whether the 17-store net reduction and shift in channel translate into profitability.
key_quotes: So my guess is that our H2 will be very, very strong.

But if you ask me, I have done enough businesses in my life to know mid-teens is a good ROCE to have for a manufacturing -driven business, so that will be the endeavor, but that is not the target that I am chasing.
So the endeavour is the same, to keep improving on this till the tailwinds persist.
We have closed taking orders for December on 31st July.
summary.management_tone: Confident and bullish on FY27 and the garmenting order book, saying Q1 was ahead of budget and last year. Cautious and evasive on specifics: declined firm garmenting EBITDA guidance, FY28 outlook and ROCE targets, citing unpredictable international trade conditions.

growth.why: Management says Q1 was ahead of budget phasing and FY27 is 'ahead of our budget' with no numeric revenue or EBITDA guidance; growth backed partly by garmenting orders booked from January, full garmenting capacity through December, and 5-7% apparel and 7-9% fabric price hikes from Q2, while branded EBO network shrinks by 34 net.
